recommendation: Keep the fix. It preserves the applied f202 example while removing guidance tied to a retired element; broader questions about principal-diagnosis codes or Encounter.diagnosis.use binding content should remain with active PA terminology/modeling work, not this STU3 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-14758 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and asked to address principal diagnosis handling for Encounter.diagnosis.role by removing the redundant encounter-primaryDiagnosis extension and updating example f202 rather than adding a new principalDiagnosis role code.
initial_application: Git commit c1e9ac08c9 applied the old GF#14758 change by removing the encounter-primaryDiagnosis extension from source/encounter/encounter-example-f202-20130128.xml and adding a second Encounter.diagnosis entry with Chief Complaint coding and rank=1. Current source and Extension Pack searches found no remaining encounter-primaryDiagnosis or encounter-relatedCondition extension definition to fix in this checkout.
additional_context: Later Published Encounter decisions changed the model: FHIR-16148 redesigned Encounter.reason and Encounter.diagnosis for R5, removed Encounter.diagnosis.rank, and moved billing ranking guidance to Account; FHIR-38807 completed remaining Encounter text cleanup; FHIR-38784 later made Encounter.diagnosis.use repeat. These later decisions made the old f202 comment stale even though the example's Chief Complaint diagnosis use coding remains in the current example.
reconciliation: Updated source/encounter/encounter-example-f202-20130128.xml so the comment describes the entry as a diagnosis classified with the Chief Complaint diagnosis use code, without reintroducing rank or changing the broader Encounter diagnosis model.
source_changes: source/encounter/encounter-example-f202-20130128.xml: changed the f202 comment from stale role=CC/rank=1 wording to current Chief Complaint diagnosis use wording.
